thesis_health.reason: Demographic demand, aging-in-place adoption and labor-productivity needs remain durable, while reimbursement, affordability, workforce costs and valuation create material dispersion.

scenarios.description: Utilization expands while technology, reimbursement, occupancy gains and productivity improvements allow leading companies to compound earnings and cash flow.
entry_conditions: Utilization, reimbursement, productivity and outcomes improve together
Labor-saving technology produces measurable customer returns
Company valuations remain supported by per-share cash-flow growth
exit_conditions: Reimbursement falls materially behind labor costs

scenarios.description: Aging demand remains durable, but labor, reimbursement, affordability, regulation and valuation constrain returns and create wide company-level dispersion.
entry_conditions: Operating performance varies substantially by business model
exit_conditions: Broad productivity and reimbursement improvements support a bull transition
Multiple assumptions deteriorate enough to support a bear transition

scenarios.description: Funding pressure, labor shortages, quality failures, affordability constraints or therapeutic disruption materially weaken current business models.
entry_conditions: Demand growth fails to create sustainable cash flow
Quality, regulatory or affordability failures spread

decision.summary: Maintain the aging theme and monitor ResMed, Stryker and Welltower using company-specific valuation thresholds.
required_actions: Review ResMed fiscal 2026 results after release
Monitor Stryker cyber recovery and orthopedic procedure growth
Monitor Welltower occupancy, acquisition integration and valuation

developments.title: Global aging continues to expand the structural demand base
developments.fact: The global population aged 60 and older is projected to rise from approximately 1.1 billion in 2023 to 1.4 billion by 2030.
developments.interpretation: Confirms long-duration demand but does not guarantee attractive provider economics.

developments.title: Care labor scarcity supports productivity demand
developments.fact: Home-health and personal-care aide employment is projected to grow 17% from 2024 through 2034, with approximately 765800 openings annually.
developments.interpretation: Supports automation and workflow technology while increasing wage and staffing pressure for operators.

developments.title: Calendar-year 2026 home-health reimbursement remains constrained
developments.fact: CMS implemented a permanent negative 1.023% behavioral adjustment to the national standardized 30-day home-health payment rate.
developments.interpretation: Aging-in-place demand does not automatically produce favorable provider margins.

developments.title: Senior-housing occupancy and operating leverage strengthened
developments.fact: Welltower reported 20.5% seniors-housing operating same-store NOI growth, 330 basis points of occupancy growth and 5.2% RevPOR growth.
developments.interpretation: Senior-housing fundamentals are strong, although current valuation embeds substantial continued execution.

developments.title: Home respiratory and sleep-care economics improved
developments.fact: ResMed reported 11% revenue growth, 21% non-GAAP EPS growth, 290 basis points of gross-margin expansion and 554 million dollars of quarterly operating cash flow.
developments.interpretation: Connected home-care devices and recurring consumables provide scalable aging-related return engines.

developments.title: Orthopedic and procedure demand remained strong
developments.fact: Stryker reported 9.0% organic sales growth, 8.6% Orthopaedics growth and 17.9% adjusted EPS growth.
developments.interpretation: Mobility procedures, implants, robotics and hospital-productivity demand remain supported.

scorecard.name: Older populations increase demand for care and support
scorecard.assessment: Strong demographic, utilization, senior-housing and procedure evidence.

scorecard.name: Funding and reimbursement remain adequate
scorecard.assessment: Funding is adequate in selected categories, but home-health adjustments and affordability constrain operators.

scorecard.name: Labor scarcity increases productivity demand
scorecard.assessment: Workforce projections strongly support automation, robotics and workflow investment.

scorecard.name: Home and community settings gain share
scorecard.assessment: Connected devices and home-based care are growing, although reimbursement economics are uneven.

scorecard.name: Chronic-disease management remains a durable need
scorecard.assessment: Sleep, mobility, rehabilitation, diagnostics and recurring care remain supported.

scorecard.name: Leading providers maintain quality and trust
scorecard.assessment: Strong operators exist, but quality, regulatory, cyber and execution risks remain material.

catalysts.confirmation_test: Payment updates support access and sustainable provider economics

publication.headline: Aging demand remains intact, but valuation and reimbursement determine investability
publication.summary: The initial Aging Economy baseline ranks ResMed, Stryker and Welltower as the leading company opportunities, with ResMed offering the strongest current valuation support.
